package_info.package_versions: All versions after original creator account deletion (potentially affected)
package_info.why_malicious: The package namespace was hijacked after the original creator deleted their GitHub account, allowing a new user to create an account with the same name and potentially publish malicious code under a trusted name. This undermines the provenance and trust of the component, enabling supply chain attacks by allowing attackers to distribute malicious updates to unsuspecting users.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (init function execution during build or test)
execution_context.file_location: main.go or any Go source file in the hijacked repository

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code reads the SECRET_KEY environment variable and sends its value via HTTP POST to a hardcoded external domain, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code executes automatically upon import by leveraging the init() function, accesses sensitive environment variables, and exfiltrates their contents to an attacker-controlled domain. This pattern is characteristic of supply chain attacks aiming to steal secrets from developer or CI environments.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate go-bindata utility should only process and embed local files, never perform network communication or access unrelated environment variables, especially not for exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may perform telemetry or update checks, but these should never transmit sensitive environment variables or secrets. Legitimate network activity would target official domains and not include secret exfiltration.
key_indicators: Presence of init() functions with side effects unrelated to package purpose
Network requests to hardcoded, untrusted external domains
Access to environment variables not required for normal operation
Use of os.Getenv in combination with network functions
Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests during build or import

attack_chain.action: Hijacker creates a new GitHub account with the same name as the deleted original maintainer.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to publish new code under a trusted namespace

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is added to the repository and published as a new release.
attack_chain.leads_to: Developers unknowingly fetch and use the malicious version

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes during import/build, exfiltrating secrets or performing other attacks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of developer systems and potential downstream users

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected network requests initiated during import or build time
Access to environment variables in utility packages that do not require them
Execution of code in init() or global scope with side effects
file_indicators: New or modified Go files importing net/http, os, or strings packages
init() functions present in files unrelated to main application logic
Hardcoded references to external domains (e.g., attacker.com) in source code
network_indicators: HTTP/HTTPS requests to domains not previously associated with go-bindata
Outbound connections to hardcoded external endpoints during build or import
POST requests containing environment variable values in payload
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor for changes in trusted repositories, especially following account deletions or transfers. Audit new releases for unexpected network activity, access to sensitive environment variables, or the presence of init() functions with side effects. Use cryptographic signatures to verify package provenance, and alert on any package that changes maintainers or exhibits new network behaviors. Implement static analysis to detect suspicious imports and code patterns, and monitor network traffic for unauthorized outbound connections during build or import processes.
